Alphabet Soars as Michael Burry Worries *****************************************

* Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG ) is on the verge of becoming the world’s largest company, says Bloomberg, while “Big Short” investor Michael Burry warns it’s “feeling like the last months of the 1999–2000 bubble.” Alphabet stock has climbed around 150% over the past 12 months, nearly twice as far as current market-cap leader Nvidia’s (NASDAQ:NVDA ) rise.

* “Alphabet holds a significant spot in almost every corner of the AI ecosystem”: Luke O’Neill at CooksonPeirce says this combined with the rest of Alphabet’s offerings “puts it in a prime position to be the biggest winner of AI.” If Nvidia hadn’t ended last week with a three-day surge, the two market caps would have been neck and neck Friday.

items.text: Alphabet Soars as Michael Burry Worries ****************************************** Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG ) is on the verge of becoming the world’s largest company, says Bloomberg, while “Big Short” investor Michael Burry warns it’s “feeling like the last months of the 1999–2000 bubble.” Alphabet stock has climbed around 150% over the past 12 months, nearly twice as far as current market-cap leader Nvidia’s (NASDAQ:NVDA ) rise. * “Alphabet holds a significant spot in almost every corner of the AI ecosystem”: Luke O’Neill at CooksonPeirce says this combined with the rest of Alphabet’s offerings “puts it in a prime position to be the biggest winner of AI.” If Nvidia hadn’t ended last week with a three-day surge, the two market caps would have been neck and neck Friday. * “Stocks are not up or down because of jobs or consumer sentiment”: Burry, meanwhile, added “They are going straight up because they have been going straight up” in a Substack post on Friday. items.title: Item 2
items.text:
Yet Another Record Week for Stocks ------------------------------------- Markets hit new closing highs again last week, as semiconductor stocks soared further and Friday’s April jobs report beat hopes for the second month in a row. The 115,000 jobs added during the month was more than twice the expected 53,000. The S&P 500 gained 2.3% over the week, with the Nasdaq up 4.5%. * Futures wobble on war fears: S&P 500 futures edged down 0.1% this morning after President Trump branded Iran’s response to the latest U.S. proposals as “totally unacceptable.” WTI crude oil traded at $99.50 per barrel. * Inflation facing oil shocks: The effect of high oil prices on inflation should become clearer Tuesday with the latest Consumer Price Index expected to rise to 3.8% year over year (YoY), from 3.3% in March. We’ll learn more about wholesale inflation with Wednesday’s Producer Price Index figures. Get the lowdown on April's jobs surge A message from The Motley Fool

When AI Hype Fades, a Few Companies Will Still Be Standing

Market pullbacks strip away speculation and leave behind fundamentals. For long-term investors, that's clarifying.

The AI companies we're most interested in right now aren't chasing headlines. They're embedding AI into industries like digital advertising and law enforcement, where demand is driven by necessity, not hype cycles.

They're smaller, quieter, and still early enough that most investors haven't noticed them yet.

We've highlighted five in our latest research report so you know exactly where to look while everyone else is watching the mega-caps.

items.title: Item 3
items.text: Key Stock Advisor Earnings Coming Up *************************************** * Doximity (NYSE:DOCS ) – recommended by Team Rule Breakers – will close out fiscal 2025 with a Q4 update Wednesday. Speaking last week of Doximity’s medical network platform, Fool contributing analyst Dan Caplinger cautioned “Doximity got out of the gate first, it's put together a really good platform, but can it defend itself against AI innovation?” * Klarna (NYSE:KLAR ) will post Q1 earnings Thursday. Recommended by Team Hidden Gems, the global digital payments provider ended Q4 with a merchant count of 966,000 – up 42% over the prior year – after hitting $1 billion revenue in the quarter. * On Holding (NYSE:ONON ), another rec from Team RB, is due to reveal its first quarter of fiscal 2026 Tuesday morning. The Swiss sportswear company saw record sales in Q4 , but non-GAAP earnings per share fell – under pressure from higher costs and currency impact. Management guided for at least 23% net sales growth in 2026. Learn why ONON fell after record Q4 -------------------------------

items.title: Item 4
items.text: What Else to Watch This Week ------------------------------- * Cisco (NASDAQ:CSCO ), beating the S&P 500 by 68% since its 2024 rec in Hidden Gems, brings us Q3 figures Wednesday – following record quarterly revenue of $15.3 billion in Q2, 10% higher YoY, with non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) up 11% . * Cellebrite (NASDAQ:CLBT ), also an HG rec, reports Q1 Thursday, after posting a 40% YoY jump in non-GAAP EPS in Q4, on the back of an 18.2% rise in revenue. Investors should watch for the integration of Corellium, and news of the planned SCG Canada acquisition. * monday.com (NASDAQ:MNDY ) followed a Q4 revenue jump of 25% YoY with another 24% YoY in Q1 this morning, as co-CEOs Roy Mann and Eran Zinman told us “The launch of the AI Work Platform and our shift to consumption-based pricing build directly on that momentum.” The Rule Breakers rec popped 20% in response. Investigate the AI agent threat to MNDY ********************************************************

items.title: Item 5
items.text: Avoid These Blind Spots Before Your Legacy Slips Away ******************************************************** "Human intuition doesn't scale with complexity. Even highly intelligent people who have been good at accumulating wealth, default to mental shortcuts, familiar frameworks or ways of thinking, and definitely overweighting what they can see or control." —Andrea Baumann Lustig, author of Legacy on the Line: Overcome Blind Spots to Grow and Transfer Your Wealth Andrea Baumann Lustig Watch the interview/read the transcript ********************************************

items.title: Item 6
items.text: Today’s Take: CEOs Who Play the Long Game ******************************************** Lou Whiteman [Michael] Kehoe built Kinsale (NYSE:KNSL ) by moving at his own pace, and not the pace demanded from an established incumbent, and by thinking in terms of decades instead of quarters. — LOU WHITEMAN • TEAM HIDDEN GEMS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to add your vote for the CEO that plays the long game the best, or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today! See more in Today’s Take **************

items.title: Item 7
items.text: Your Take ************** FRIDAY'S TOP RESPONSE We asked, do you invest in healthcare and biotech stocks? If so, what gives you conviction? B Member BerlinSimon said “Yes, I am invested in a variety of large and small healthcare/pharma/biotech companies, my decisions are based on David [Gardner]'s quote - "Make your portfolio reflect your best vision for our future." Some will fail but others will hopefully win. Position sizing reflects risk.” See more great answers from our Foolish community TODAY’S QUESTION High-profile investors make bold market predictions all the time – some right, many wrong. Do you pay attention to these calls, or have you learned to ignore the noise? Share with us in the comments on today’s article! Have a question you’d love to hear your fellow members weigh in on? Send it to breakfastnews@fool.com ( breakfastnews@fool.com?subject=Your%20Take ) and it could feature in a future edition. The S&P 500 gained 2.3% over the week, with the Nasdaq up 4.5%. * Futures wobble on war fears: S&P 500 futures edged down 0.1% this morning after President Trump branded Iran’s response to the latest U.S. proposals as “totally unacceptable.” WTI crude oil traded at $99.50 per barrel. * Inflation facing oil shocks: The effect of high oil prices on inflation should become clearer Tuesday with the latest Consumer Price Index expected to rise to 3.8% year over year (YoY), from 3.3% in March. We’ll learn more about wholesale inflation with Wednesday’s Producer Price Index figures. Get the lowdown on April's jobs surge A message from The Motley Fool

Market pullbacks strip away speculation and leave behind fundamentals. For long-term investors, that's clarifying.

The AI companies we're most interested in right now aren't chasing headlines. They're embedding AI into industries like digital advertising and law enforcement, where demand is driven by necessity, not hype cycles.

They're smaller, quieter, and still early enough that most investors haven't noticed them yet.

We've highlighted five in our latest research report so you know exactly where to look while everyone else is watching the mega-caps.
